standard.title: Create arts works that communicate ideas
standard.description: create arts works that communicate ideas
standard.prior_knowledge: No formal prior Drama curriculum. Students bring imaginative play, storytelling through objects and movement, and early experience using voice, gesture and repurposed materials to express ideas.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create arts works — including dramatic play, scenes and puppetry — that communicate ideas drawn from imagination and experience.

nodes.label: Ideas from imagination and experience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify an idea from play, a story or personal experience to express through making.
nodes.minimum_width: One example: a student names or shows what their dramatic play or object manipulation is about.
nodes.typical_width: Students draw on stories, characters or personal experience to identify what they want to make and communicate; they can describe their idea simply to a partner or teacher.
wider: Students explore multiple potential ideas across different starting points (e.g. a story, an object, a place) before choosing one to develop
Students ask 'what if' questions to extend a familiar story into a new scenario
nodes.hinge_reason: Without a communicative intent — even a simple one — students produce activity rather than art-making; the next node (choosing ways to express the idea) has no anchor.

response_modes.reason: Use teacher-in-role or guided questioning ('What's happening? What happens next?') to help students find and name an idea before they begin making.
Offer a range of imaginative entry points — objects, boxes, puppets, images — so students who don't connect with story-based prompts can engage through material play.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of starting points available — material play, animation, character imaginings, personal experience, cultural stories — is genuinely rich; width here builds the habit of finding communicative intent across many contexts.
success_criteria: Student can name or show (through action or words) what their drama or artwork is about
Student's making has a recognisable intent — it is not purely random activity

nodes.label: Choosing ways to express the idea
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select and use at least one mode (movement, voice, object/puppet, image) to express their idea.
nodes.minimum_width: One mode used intentionally: e.g. student uses a puppet to retell a story, or uses movement/voice to show a character.
nodes.typical_width: Students experiment with using voice, movement, objects or repurposed materials to express their idea; they try more than one approach and choose one that communicates their intent.
wider: Students combine two modes (e.g. voice and movement, or puppet and voice-over) in the same piece
Students explore how digital devices (e.g. recording voice) can extend how they share an idea

response_modes.reason: Provide a range of materials, props and modes for students to try; encourage experimentation without locking in a single approach early.

success_criteria: Student uses at least one mode (voice, movement, object, or image) in a way that communicates their idea to a viewer
Student can explain or show what their chosen mode is doing in the piece

nodes.label: Making and communicating
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create a simple arts work — scene, puppetry sequence, or dramatic play — that communicates an identifiable idea.
nodes.minimum_width: A short, coherent piece (even 30–60 seconds) in which the idea is legible to another person without full explanation.
nodes.typical_width: Students create a scene, puppet sequence, chant, or dramatic play using repurposed materials or props; the piece has a recognisable beginning, moment of action, and ending; a peer or teacher can identify the idea being communicated.
wider: Students create a piece that responds to a specific question or problem ('What message could a character send?', 'What happens in this space?')
Students create a work drawing on stories from their cultural community or family experience
Students use digital capture (photo sequence, voice recording) to document and share their making

response_modes.reason: This is the integration point — idea, mode and making come together. Teacher role is to scaffold coherence: 'What is this piece about? What do you want someone watching to think or feel?'

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of cultural stories, community contexts and material starting points available to Foundation students is broad; students who engage widely here build a richer repertoire of communicative possibilities.
success_criteria: Student creates a piece in which an idea is communicated through at least one arts mode
A peer or teacher can identify the idea without needing the student to fully explain it
Student can describe one thing they did to communicate their idea
